events.title: Vitiges ends his year-long siege of Rome
events.description: The Ostrogothic king Vitiges ended the siege of Rome, which Byzantine forces under General Belisarius had held against his numerically superior army since March 537. The siege, the first major clash of the Gothic War, played a decisive role in its course.
events.html: The Ostrogothic king Vitiges ended the siege of Rome, which Byzantine forces under General Belisarius had held against his numerically superior army since March 537. The siege, the first major clash of the Gothic War, played a decisive role in its course.

events.title: Odo of Châtillon elected Pope Urban II
events.description: Elected at Terracina while a rival pope held Rome, Urban II continued Gregory VII's reforms. In 1095 he preached the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont.
events.html: Elected at Terracina while a rival pope held Rome, Urban II continued Gregory VII's reforms. In 1095 he preached the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont.

events.title: Konrad von Wallenrode is elected Grand Master of the Teutonic Order
events.description: Konrad von Wallenrode was elected the 24th Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, the supreme head of the order, and served until 1393.
events.html: Konrad von Wallenrode was elected the 24th Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, the supreme head of the order, and served until 1393.

events.title: Spanish forces begin the siege of Maastricht in the Dutch Revolt
events.description: The siege of Maastricht, a battle of the Eighty Years' War between rebels in the Habsburg Netherlands and the Spanish government, began and lasted until 1 July. It ended in a Spanish victory.
events.html: The siege of Maastricht, a battle of the Eighty Years' War between rebels in the Habsburg Netherlands and the Spanish government, began and lasted until 1 July. It ended in a Spanish victory.

events.title: Ignatius of Loyola and Francis Xavier are canonized as saints
events.description: Ignatius of Loyola, who with six companions had founded the Society of Jesus and was its first Superior General, was canonized together with Francis Xavier, the Jesuit co-founder who led the first Christian mission to Japan.
events.html: Ignatius of Loyola, who with six companions had founded the Society of Jesus and was its first Superior General, was canonized together with Francis Xavier, the Jesuit co-founder who led the first Christian mission to Japan.

events.title: Charles II grants New Netherland to the Duke of York
events.description: The King granted his brother James lands between the Connecticut and Delaware rivers, then held by the Dutch. English ships seized New Amsterdam that August and renamed it New York.
events.html: The King granted his brother James lands between the Connecticut and Delaware rivers, then held by the Dutch. English ships seized New Amsterdam that August and renamed it New York.

events.title: Juliette Gordon Low founds the Girl Scouts in Savannah
events.description: Inspired by the Guide movement she had seen in Britain, Low gathered 18 girls for the first meeting of the American Girl Guides. Renamed the Girl Scouts in 1913, it has had tens of millions of members.
events.html: Inspired by the Guide movement she had seen in Britain, Low gathered 18 girls for the first meeting of the American Girl Guides. Renamed the Girl Scouts in 1913, it has had tens of millions of members.

events.title: German troops march into Austria
events.description: The Wehrmacht crossed the border unopposed and was greeted by cheering crowds. The next day Austria was declared part of the German Reich, the Anschluss that Versailles had forbidden.
events.html: The Wehrmacht crossed the border unopposed and was greeted by cheering crowds. The next day Austria was declared part of the German Reich, the Anschluss that Versailles had forbidden.

events.title: Truman announces the Truman Doctrine
events.description: Asking Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey, Harry Truman pledged to support 'free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation'. The doctrine framed US Cold War policy of containment.
events.html: Asking Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey, Harry Truman pledged to support 'free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation'. The doctrine framed US Cold War policy of containment.

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web
events.description: At CERN in Geneva, Berners-Lee circulated 'Information Management: A Proposal' for a hypertext system linking documents across computers. His supervisor called it 'vague but exciting'.

song: Byzantine Christians; the Eastern Orthodox Church
A slow, sad hymn for Holy Week by Kassia, a nun of Constantinople in the 800s, the only woman whose music the Byzantine Church sang.
